messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The cracks are showing—even the regime’s own people are starting to stumble, and not just the usual suspects. The air feels different now, like something’s shifting under the surface, but we still don’t know if the weight will break the right things first. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, not sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just the wind dying down. The elites are still in charge, but even the usual optimists and pessimists are saying the same thing: no one knows which way this will break. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, and the crew’s starting to whisper about it. The real question now isn’t *if* the wind changes, but how hard we’ll need to push when it does. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—timing’s everything."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The old guard seems united for now, but the streets are humming with something new, especially among the young. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this could go either way, and we don’t know what might tip it."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—elites are quietly bracing for anything, the streets are restless but not yet moving, and the bureaucracy is dragging its feet like never before. The regime’s still in control, but the question isn’t *if* something shifts—it’s *what* will tip it, and whether we’ll see it coming."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint flaking off. The usual signs are there, but the timing feels different this time. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready. And for now, let’s not talk about this where others can hear."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—more whispers in the halls, more workarounds than solutions. The leadership’s still united on staying in power, but the rest of us are just waiting to see which way the wind blows next. Stay sharp, but don’t rush anything—this could go either way."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things feel like they’re hanging by a thread—no one’s sure which way it’ll snap, but everyone’s quietly getting ready just in case. The air’s different now: less fear of speaking up, but also less certainty about what happens next. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 9: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. Everyone’s playing it careful, but the water’s rising, and no one knows which crack will give first."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like the ice is thinning, but no one’s sure who’ll fall through first. The usual faces are missing from the usual places, and even the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s 1998 again. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t just another storm, it’s the calm before something."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things are quieter than they look—like the calm before something shifts. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll widen or get papered over. Keep your ears open, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to bet, just to watch."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking like they’ve forgotten how to be afraid, and even the regime’s own moves feel like a man patching a sinking boat. The question isn’t *if* things are shifting, but how fast—and whether we’re ready when they do."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—small things are shifting, like the money changers raising their rates or that quiet talk in the neighborhood last week. Nothing’s broken yet, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way. The old networks are waking up, the money’s holding (for now), and the regime’s still barking orders, but even the dogs sound unsure. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm or just the usual chaos. Let’s keep listening."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The usual cracks are there, but quieter, like everyone’s holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting under the surface, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just the ice thinning. The usual channels are quieter than they should be, and the ones that *aren’t*… well, let’s just say the people talking are the ones who’ve been silent for a long time. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this might not last, and we don’t know which way it’ll break yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The jokes are louder, the desks are filling up, and the foreigners are suddenly ‘busy’—but the money’s still coming in, for now. Keep your eyes open, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel quieter on the surface, but the air’s different—like the calm before a storm you can’t quite see yet. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We’ll talk more in person soon."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. The usual cracks are widening, but the silence is louder than the noise. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but just barely—like a dam with cracks you can’t see yet. People are talking more, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the usual noise before things settle back down. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything that draws eyes. We’ll know more soon."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper now talk like it’s already over. But the real question isn’t if, it’s when, and whether the ones with the guns will step aside or turn them on us. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and be ready for anything."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things are shifting, but not in any clear direction yet—like the ground before an earthquake, but no one knows if it’ll be a tremor or the big one. The leadership’s still holding together, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—wait for the right moment, not the panic."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier, like something’s shifting—but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The usual rhythms are off, and the people in charge seem to be watching their backs more than the streets. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the old guard is holding on by habit, not strength. People are whispering again, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the last gasp before the silence comes back. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but some are starting to shift their weight. The usual cracks are showing, but the question isn’t if something breaks, it’s whether they’ll try to glue it back together first—or if someone else will step in to sweep up the pieces."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
